newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BURTON SAYS DEMERGER ON COURSE.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BURTON SAYS DEMERGER ON COURSE.

text.p: British fashion retailer Burton Group Plc said on Thursday the loss of finance director Andrew Higginson to Britain's top food retailer Tesco Plc would not mean any disruption to plans to demerge department store Debenhams.
Burton chief executive John Hoerner said it was a disappointment to lose Higginson, but he was not leaving until November by which time most of the work preparing for the demerger would be complete.
Hoerner told Reuters by telephone Higginson had received an offer he felt he could not turn down.

Nigel Hall, who will replace Higginson, has worked with Burton since 1984. He was recently made director of the demerger process with responsibility for overall management of the commercial and statutory work required.
Hoerner said he was pleased there was a suitable candidate in house to take over Higginson's job.
"Nigel was actually someone I was going to lose in the demerger because I didn't have a good enough job for him," he said.
Burton announced plans to spin off Debenhams last month.
The group said in a statement that Hall had been appointed to the board with immediate effect and between now and November would continue in his responsibility as director of the demerger process.
Hall will remain finance director of the re-named Burton Group which will operate the group's multiples businesses.
At Tesco's Higginson, 40, will succeed David Reid, who is currently finance director and deputy chairman of the supermarket group, in November.

Higginson has been finance director at Burton since 1994. Before that he was finance director at Laura Ashley Holdings Plc from 1990 to 1994, having joined from Guinness Brewing International where he was also finance director.
